# New-ZbxUserGroup

## SYNOPSIS

Creates a user group.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxUserGroup [[-Name] <string>] [-DebugMode <bool>] [-GuiAccess <ZabbixGuiAccess>] [-UsersStatus <ZabbixGroupStatus>] [-UserDirectoryId <ulong>] [-MfaStatus <bool>] [-MfaId <ulong>] [-Right <ZabbixUserGroupRightRequest[]>] [-HostGroupRight <ZabbixUserGroupHostGroupRightRequest[]>] [-TemplateGroupRight <ZabbixUserGroupTemplateGroupRightRequest[]>] [-TagFilter <ZabbixUserGroupTagFilterRequest[]>] [-User <ZabbixReference<ZabbixUser>[]>] [-Proxy <ZabbixReference<ZabbixProxy>[]>] [-ProxyGroup <ZabbixReference<ZabbixProxyGroup>[]>] [-ProxyMode <ZabbixProxyMode>] [-ProxyGroupMode <ZabbixProxyGroupMode>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A user group is a named set of users that sets their permissions on host and template groups, their frontend access and their authentication. The New-ZbxUserGroup cmdlet sends usergroup.create with one request field per parameter, then reads the new user group back with usergroup.get and writes it. The server requires -Name; -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name and wins over a parameter. -WhatIf shows what would be created, and the command needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Create a user group

```powershell
New-ZbxUserGroup -Name 'Night shift' -HostGroupRight @{ id = (Get-ZbxHostGroup -Name 'Linux servers').GroupId; permission = 2 }
```

Creates a user group named Night shift. The command writes the new user group, read back from the server.
